note.text: The scramble for Cameroon involved competing commercial and imperial ambitions, local negotiations and unequal power. German firms encouraged official protection of their interests. Some coastal rulers had previously sought British protection, while British official responses did not secure control before the German action. In July 1884, treaties and a German flag ceremony marked the coastal claim. This was a beginning of colonial expansion, not proof that every inland community had agreed or that all resistance had ended.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: The scramble for Cameroon involved competing commercial and imperial ambitions, local negotiations and unequal power. German firms encouraged official protection of their interests. Some coastal rulers had previously sought British protection, while British official responses did not secure control before the German action. In July {1884}, treaties and a German flag ceremony marked the coastal claim. This was a beginning of colonial expansion, not proof that every inland community had agreed or that all resistance had ended.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: The German-Duala treaty conventionally dated {12} July {1884} and Nachtigal's flag raising on {14} July must be distinguished. A document signed by particular rulers had a specific scope. The later extension of German control required further diplomacy, coercion and military action. Do not compress these different stages into one event covering the whole modern territory.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Build a sequence: prior contact and rivalry, coastal negotiations, imperial claim and inland expansion. Ask whose authority a treaty could actually bind. Compare the wording of a claim with the extent of control on the ground and with evidence of dissent.
